subject: Audit & access log export options, deletion SLAs — BlueHarbor Health
messages:
From: Maya Singh <maya.singh@blueharbor.health>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood-inference.com>
Date: 2025-08-04T16:12:00Z
Subject: Questions on audit/access log retention + exports

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. BlueHarbor is doing a pre-audit review and we need to confirm how Redwood handles audit and access logs for hosted customers. A few specific asks so we can sign off with our compliance team:

- Retention windows by log type (access/auth events, admin/audit events, request payloads including prompts/response bodies). Our base requirement is 7 years for audit traces, but we understand payload retention may differ for privacy reasons.
- Export capabilities: can we pull an account-scoped export for arbitrary time ranges? Formats? Do you support NDJSON/Parquet and is there an API for bulk export?
- Residency: are exported bundles guaranteed to be region-resident (US/EU) and do exports include a manifest showing storage locations?
- Deletion workflow & proof: when BlueHarbor requests deletion of logs for a dataset, what is the SLA to permanently remove records and can you provide a signed proof-of-deletion or tamper-evident manifest?

We are HIPAA-adjacent, so preserving both the chain-of-custody and the ability to demonstrate deletion to auditors is high priority. If you have a short mock export/manifest we can review that would be ideal.

Thanks,
Maya
Maya Singh
Sr. Security Ops
BlueHarbor Health

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood-inference.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya.singh@blueharbor.health>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood-inference.com>
Date: 2025-08-04T18:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Questions on audit/access log retention + exports

Hi Maya — thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise summary of what Redwood provides for hosted accounts; I’ve looped in Evelyn (Security) for any policy nuance, and will follow up with a technical export sample from our logs team.

Retention (hosted, default tiers):
- Access/auth events (login, token exchange, API key usage): default 365 days; extended retention (up to 7 years) available as an add-on contract for enterprise customers.
- Audit/admin events (role changes, policy updates, config diffs): retained 2 years by default; enterprise retention up to 7 years available.
- Request/response payloads (prompt text, full response): retained 90 days by default for hosted API to limit sensitive data exposure. Payload retention beyond 90 days requires explicit configuration and contract terms (we recommend Private or Dedicated for long-term payload retention).

Export capabilities:
- UI: Console -> Logs -> Export: ad-hoc exports for an account and time range. Formats: CSV (row-oriented), NDJSON (newline-delimited JSON), Parquet (large-volume optimized).
- API: /v1/logs/exports POST to create export job; returns job_id and status endpoint. Exports are delivered to a customer-requested S3 bucket or ephemeral signed URL (48h).
- Bundles include: export_manifest.json (file list, record counts, UTC timestamps, SHA256 hashes) and schema file (redwood_log_schema.md).

Residency & encryption:
- Exports are generated in the region that hosts the account (US / eu-west-1 / ap-southeast-1). If you request cross-region delivery we’ll note that in the manifest; default behavior is region-bound output.
- All export artifacts are encrypted at rest (AES-256) and in transit (TLS 1.2+).

Deletion workflow & proof:
- Hosted: deletion requests create a purge operation. Items are soft-deleted immediately and then scheduled for irreversible purge within 30 days unless a legal hold is present.
- Dedicated/Private: customers can opt for immediate irrevocable deletion (customer-managed) or a vendor-assisted purge with a mutually agreed SLA.
- Proof: we can provide a signed export_manifest indicating the pre-purge object manifest and, after purge, a deletion_manifest containing S3 object IDs, purge timestamps, and SHA256 hashes of the deleted bundles, signed by Redwood’s security team (PGP-signed text file).

SLA for bulk exports: typical turnaround is 4–24 hours for datasets < 1TB, 24–72 hours for larger requests (dependent on queue and retention tier). For urgent forensic requests we offer expedited processing as part of enterprise plans.

Attachment: I’ll send a small mock export (CSV + manifest) in a follow-up email from our logs team.

If helpful, we can schedule a 30–45 minute walk-through with Steph from infra to go over schema and API.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Head of Sales, Enterprise Accounts
Redwood Inference

Jordan — this is helpful. A couple quick clarifications:

- For payloads: when you say 90 days default, are prompts/redactions that contain PHI treated differently? Can we request redaction at export time (e.g., redact PII fields before export)?
- For proof-of-deletion: would the signed deletion_manifest be sufficient for our auditors? Do you include a hash chain or timestamped signature from an independent KMS to make it tamper-evident?

We may prefer an export that strips free-text prompts and instead includes metadata (e.g., request_id, user_id hash, timestamp) for long-term retention. Is that supported today, or would it be a product request?

Thanks — Maya

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood-inference.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya.singh@blueharbor.health>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood-inference.com>
Date: 2025-08-07T23:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Questions on audit/access log retention + exports — technical detail + next steps

Hi Maya / Jordan,

Thanks for the clear scope. Below are technical details and options we can offer today (hosted) and for Dedicated/Private deployments. I’ve attached a small mock export (audit_export_sample.csv) and a sample export_manifest.json to this thread.

Retention by log class (clarified):
- Authentication / access events: 1 year default (searchable), extendable to 7 years under enterprise add-on. Contains: event_id, timestamp (UTC), principal_id (SHA256), action, ip, region, outcome. No free-text prompts.
- Admin/audit events (RBAC changes, policy updates): 2 years default, enterprise up to 7 years. Contains structured diffs and actor metadata.
- Request payloads (prompts/responses): 90 days default. For hosted customers we do not retain full-text payloads beyond 90 days unless explicitly contracted. For HIPAA workloads we recommend Dedicated/Private where customer controls retention.

Redaction and export-time transformations:
- Today (hosted): we support export-time field projection and removal of specified fields (e.g., prompt_text, response_text) so you can produce an export that includes request_id, user_id_hash, model, tokens_consumed, but not free-text. This is available via the export API with a fields parameter.
- We also support pattern-based PII redaction in exports for common PII fields (emails, SSNs) but not for arbitrary free-text; custom redaction rules can be scoped as a professional services engagement.

Proof-of-deletion and tamper-evidence:
- Deletion_manifest: after purge we generate a deletion_manifest.json with the following: objects_deleted (list of export object paths), SHA256 of each object pre-delete, deletion_timestamp (UTC), and our key_id. That manifest is signed with Redwood’s private key (PGP) and we include a signature block.
- For stronger compliance: we can notarize the manifest with a timestamping authority (TSA) and include a KMS-backed HMAC chain if required (this is part of enterprise compliance add-on).

Export mechanics & SLAs:
- API: POST /v1/logs/exports {account_id, start_ts, end_ts, format: [csv|ndjson|parquet], fields: [...], destination: {s3_bucket | presigned_url}}
- Status polling: GET /v1/logs/exports/{job_id} returns state (pending | running | ready | failed) and a presigned delivery URL when ready.
- Typical times: small exports (<100M rows) usually ready in 4–6 hours; 100M–1B rows 24–48 hours; >1B rows 48–120 hours.

Residency nuance: hosted exports are generated in-account region. If you request cross-region replication we will note that in the export_manifest and in the delivery descriptor.

Immediate next steps I recommend:
1) I’ll produce a sample export for BlueHarbor that omits all free-text fields and includes user_id hashed and request_id. (attachment: audit_export_sample.csv).
2) BlueHarbor to confirm whether you want PGP-signed deletion manifests + TSA notarization as part of the SLA.
3) If you require payload retention beyond 90 days or guaranteed immediate purge on request, we can draft a Dedicated plan (we have a template SOW for log retention/compliance work).

If helpful, I’m available for a 30-minute call Thursday PST to walk through the export schema and a live mock export.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Staff Infra Engineer, Logs & Runtime
Redwood Inference
